findings.claim: The TB-26 ruling (b)-(c) does not fix the C-3 stop on an ordinary v9 run. It says an attempt stops counting as running once its 'execution capability is revoked (stopP 38)'. But stopP R04 (line 38) is the limited revocation, and A1 limits that to held Replan or certified slot phases. An ordinary running run, with no held slot, gets no revocation fact at all: its only Stop route needs native cancel and SchedulerStop, which are D06 sources that v9 lacks (Q-12). So under ruling (b) every attempt still in flight on an ordinary run stays 'running', and the C-3 stop stays pending forever. That is the failure the ruling was meant to prevent. The ruling needs a writer v9 does not have. The §3.3 and §3.4 rows that say 'capability revoked -> quiet -> stopped' rest on the same step.
findings.verified_evidence: EP-127 @A1 Executor_Protocol.md 8937-8938: 'ordinary idle has only the ordinary Stop route, whose native cancel and SchedulerStop sources are not supplied here'. stopP @A1 line 19 (R02, ordinary idle row): 'Existing ordinary StopResult is available only from its genuine original native cancel and SchedulerStop sources. This supplement does not fill those dependencies.' stopP 58: goal_execution_revoked (the only thing a bare Goal Stop gives) is 'a type distinction, never proof of native work'. stopP 62: execution_revoked 'is distinct from merely authentic Goal Stop'. stopP 90 (R09): 'No additional durable revocation record, result or origin survives independently', so outside the slot custody nothing durable is left to prove revocation. stopP 34: 'pending wakes, delays, capacity reservations and unacknowledged dispatch facts are not zeroed … disposal, acknowledgement and effect cleanup remain their independently original operations'. The ruling does not say which admitted v9 operation releases them after a Stop. The nearest canon definition of a settled domain, EP-119's DomainCut, also needs native cancel: EP 8003 @main, observe_stopped_domain.v2 needs a 'coordinator holding Goal Stop, native cancel, SchedulerStop/inventory'. The addendum itself limits revocation to held slots ('For a v9 run in a held Replan or certified slot, the same Goal Stop drives the carried EP-127 limited revocation').
findings.suggested_repair: Re-derive TB-26 phase by phase. (i) Held Replan or certified slot: the limited revocation of stopP R04 applies, and the ruling stands. (ii) Ordinary running or idle run: name the D06-free fact that shows new execution is fenced. A candidate (prop.) is the latched Goal Stop read as goal_execution_revoked through read_run_execution_revocation.v1, together with U3 (nv8 147). This must be an explicit owner ruling, because stopP 58 says that acquisition proves no native work. Add sub-questions to TB-26/T-02 for the Executor: which admitted operation releases a capacity reservation and acknowledges or disposes of a dispatch after a Goal Stop, and whether it is admitted under goal_execution_revoked. Rewrite the §3.3 and §3.4 rows so that they are conditional on this answer.

findings.claim: The §1.5 inference that the Goal Stop latch denies every native chain method rests on misapplied text, and it leaves out canon text that points the other way. (1) nv8m 247 is the entry for submit_verification, not record_verified. The same sentence, 'Execution remains denied', also appears on read-only methods, and stopP 66 keeps those admitted ('Pure readback'). So the sentence cannot mean that the method itself is refused. (2) stopP 66 begins 'After revocation', which per OQ-01 happens only in held slot phases. (3) nv8 147 and EP-122 explicitly keep native completion after a later Stop. §1.5, §2.2 and §3.3 then say 'under every B-1 option' as though TB-28 = no were the likely answer.
findings.verified_evidence: nv8m.json @A1: line 247 is inside owner.executor.native.submit_verification.v1 (entry at 194-249); record_verified is 250-305, and its copy of the sentence is line 303. The identical text is at 759 (read_retained), 806 (read_standard) and 1053 (read_current). stopP 66 @A1: 'After revocation, no execution … Pure readback, repeated Stop, original cancellation/effect cleanup, and recovery of the exact already-held original operation retain only their original narrow capabilities.' nv8 147 @A1: 'Existing authentic native completion remains preserved if Stop arrives later … The finalizer may preserve already committed native completion after Goal Stop exactly as EP-117 requires; it does not use this exception to start new work or certify the Workflow.' EP-122, Executor_Protocol.md 8472-8473 @main and @A1: 'Existing authentic completed native effects survive later Stop as their original owner permits, but cannot authorize new work or final certification.'
findings.suggested_repair: Restate TB-28 with both readings and cite U3 ('New native work requires … no accepted Stop', nv8 147) as the operative text. Ask the owner whether submit_verification, record_verified, complete_worknode ('the finalizer') and record_failed are 'new native work' or 'native completion' under U3. Fix the nv8m line attribution. Drop stopP 66 as evidence for ordinary runs. Mark as inference, not as the likely answer, every §3.3/§3.4 row that assumes denial.

findings.claim: The note says option 2 'admits one existing canon writer' and asks the card to drop its cost line. That understates the work. Canon does not hold record_failed.v1 as a writer contract, only as a one-line dependency declaration, and canon says every such method's owner must still write its full contract. No typed failure receipt exists: the only native attempt-receipt refinement is the completion one. v9's plan also says v9 'adds two writers', so option 2 changes the v9 scope in V1 and in the plan, not only the card wording. A card that presents this as merely admitting an existing writer, with no estimate, would mislead the product decision.
findings.verified_evidence: wam.json 758 (byte-identical on main and A1): record_failed.v1 'contract' is only 'actual Verifier fail; verify_pending->failed; actual original failure receipt; no current Goal writer'. EP 7445 @main: 'Each later owner must independently establish its actual original lifecycle/source contract, native capability and complete writer/final predicates.' nwca $defs: CompletionAttemptReceipt is the only refinement of LegacyAttemptReceipt, with receipt_kind const 'worknode_completion' and status const 'completed'. No failure-receipt definition exists. storage_value_registry.json @main /families/7 (attempt_receipt) requires retry_route and rollback_route (minLength 1). v9 has no retry route whose value could fill them. v9-profile-plan.md §0 item 1: 'keeps every v8 method ID, and adds two writers'. The v7 chain writers each needed a protocol paragraph and schemas (EP-122, EP-124 @main). The note's own list of missing parts (method entry, cs5-successor argument, protocol paragraph, stored-profile route, D01 rule) already amounts to an authoring task.
findings.suggested_repair: Card wording (prop.): 'v9 writes the full contract for canon's declared failure writer record_failed.v1 (only its name and one-line purpose exist today) and installs it.' Keep an estimate, by analogy to one v7 chain writer, or say it is not yet estimated. Add the missing typed failure-receipt grammar and the retry_route/rollback_route values to the 'Missing' column. Mark v9-profile-plan §0 item 1 and V1 for revision: v9 would add three writers. Keep TB-29.

findings.claim: The TB-02 ruling calls the AttemptRecord terminal_result part of the 'authoritative' durable block source. Its Storage family is registered as deferred and not backed up. The note also says record_failed writes terminal_result and result_ref, but canon's record_failed text does not say that. The claim is inferred from complete_worknode and is not labelled 'by analogy'. The note also says storage-plan 25528-25537 gives Storage keys for the joint families, but those lines do not cover attempt_record or attempt_receipt.
findings.verified_evidence: storage_value_registry.json @main and @A1: attempt_record status 'deferred_not_build_blocking', recovery_disposition.authority_class 'compatibility_or_deferred', backup_required false, deferred_reason 'Attempt persistence behavior still depends on activation/restart evidence'. executor_worknode, executor_worknode_transition, executor_attempt_control, executor_native_operation_result, executor_original_publication_origin and attempt_receipt are 'canonical_non_rebuildable' with backup_required true. wam 758 names only 'verify_pending->failed' and 'actual original failure receipt'. The terminal_result/result_ref wording comes from nv8 173, which is about the done finalizer. storage-plan.md 25528-25537 @main lists executor_* families only. attempt_record and attempt_receipt have their own generic rows (native-v8 stored-profile-routes.json @A1: 'unchanged_generic_profiles': ['attempt_record.v1', …, 'attempt_receipt', …]).

List attempt_record as corroborating only, until its deferred row closes. Mark 'record_failed sets terminal_result/result_ref' as 'by analogy to nv8 173' and send it to the Executor with TB-29.

findings.claim: TB-12 says a run whose G4 check fails at provisional_success 'is quiet, because every required WorkNode is done (nv8 179)', and the §3.4 table says a C-3 stop on it completes. That does not follow. nv8 179 requires only the required members to be complete. It explicitly keeps failed or nonterminal members, which can be non-required ones. Quiet also needs the other four T-02 facts (dispatch, effect/tool call, reservation, mutation fence), and nothing is said about those. The same gap applies to stopped design T-18 when read for provisional_success.
findings.verified_evidence: nv8 179 @A1: publish_provisional_success 'preserves all failed or nonterminal members truthfully and cannot run when any required member is missing/nonterminal/failed.' EP 7388 @main: provisioning preserves 'exact required/optional membership'. Stopped design §2.3 input 4 lists five quiet facts, not one.
findings.suggested_repair: Say that a C-3 stop at provisional_success completes only when the TB-26 census passes. A non-required member still in_progress or verify_pending holds the stop open, in the same way (and under the same OQ-01 problem) as any other in-flight attempt. Change the §3.4 G4 row to 'yes, if the census passes'.

findings.claim: The TB-25 'no' ruling reads more into nv8 153 and nv8 145 than they say, and one §3.1 argument against option 1 does not hold. nv8 153 (U6) requires that each capture be matched with its actual value inside OriginalVerifierInput. 'Cannot be used alone' means a capture without its value. A W-B that consumed the whole OriginalVerifierInput would not use it alone. nv8 145 lets 'authentic native original owner results' extend lineage, and nv8 123 makes the verifier the owner of its result. That reads toward 'yes'. The sound basis for 'no' is owner assignment. §3.1 also says option 1 'contradicts EP 141 and nv8 129'. But the verify_pending state after a failed check exists on every v8/v9 birth whether or not W-B exists. Option 1 does not create it, and a blocked record converts nothing to success. The note also calls option 2 'required', though it rests on a proposed ruling.
findings.verified_evidence: nv8 153 @A1: 'An input capture cannot be used alone. Match all capture arrays one-to-one in original order with actual values in OriginalCompletionInput and OriginalVerifierInput.' nv8 145: 'Only installed writer branches and authentic native original owner results can extend lineage. A cause token is never proof.' nv8 123: 'Executor owns original WorkNode lifecycle and attempts; the verifier owns its actual result/evidence'. nv8 129: 'failure or cancellation evidence remains truthful and cannot be converted to success'. EP 141 @main: 'Overseer sets node status = "failed"'. EP 7445 @main (later owners must establish their own lifecycle contract). storage_value_registry @main: executor_original_input_capture is canonical_non_rebuildable with backup_required true, so an issued capture is durable.
findings.suggested_repair: Re-base TB-25 on owner assignment: the failed-check record belongs to the Executor/Overseer lifecycle owner (EP 141, nv8 123, EP 7445), not to the verifier's result. Cite nv8 145 and nv8 153 only 'by analogy', and note that nv8 145 can be read either way. Drop the EP 141/nv8 129 contradiction bullet from §3.1, or restate it as 'option 1 leaves the node untruthful, as v8 already does'. Write 'option 2 is recommended if the owners confirm TB-25 = no', not 'required' (Q-09: the trigger is Jared's decision).

findings.claim: Option 2 fixes only the 'fail' branch, yet the note says it 'fixes the blocked trigger'. record_verified refuses four kinds of result (failing, blocked, skipped, unresolved), and record_failed takes only an actual verifier 'fail'. So a verify_pending attempt stays there with no writer on v9 under option 2 in these cases: the outcome is pass but a required validator is blocked or skipped (waivers are unadmitted), the outcome is pass but required evidence is missing, or the outcome stays pending (verifier unavailable, TB-12 first half). Canon does not say whether a verifier must return 'fail' in the first two cases.
findings.verified_evidence: nv8 169 @A1: 'Failing/blocked/skipped/unresolved results cannot use this method.' wam 758: record_failed 'actual Verifier fail'. project_plan_node.schema.json 117-119 @main: outcome enum ['pending','pass','fail']. nwca 2476-2500: validator_outcome is a separate input_kind. GRS 3746 @main: 'certified requires … no failed/blocked validators; skipped validators require waivers'. nv8 129: 'waiver … remain unadmitted'.
findings.suggested_repair: State on card B-1 and in §3.2 that option 2 records only a verifier 'fail'. Other non-pass results still stand still with no record. Add an owner question for the Verifier and the Executor: does the verifier always return outcome 'fail' when a required validator is failed, blocked, skipped or unresolved, or when required evidence is missing? If not, list the remaining stalls beside the 'unavailable verifier' stall.

findings.claim: A consequence for Jared's approved C-3 answer is missed. C-3 promised that running steps 'finish or time out under their own owners' and that the stop 'never cuts a step off halfway'. Under the note's reading of TB-28 (no native completion after Stop) together with ruling (a)-(c), a step running at Stop time can never be recorded done or failed. The run is recorded stopped with the step left in_progress or verify_pending. And no v9 writer records a timeout under either option: the note itself says a dead worker leaves an attempt in_progress. So 'finish or time out' has no native record on v9. The note sends this only to the owners (TB-28). It does not flag that the approved product wording would change.
findings.verified_evidence: cards-C2-C4-20260925.md (a3-stopped-scope) line 51: 'Running steps finish or time out under their own owners, the run is recorded stopped when quiet'; line 63: 'it never cuts a step off halfway'; line 65: approved. owner-questions §2.2: 'an attempt whose worker dies stays in_progress … v8 admits no cancellation or retry writer'. nwca 2277-2380: no edge out of in_progress except to verify_pending. The addendum already treats a smaller wording change (T-24, CR-11) as needing a C-3 Decision Log note.
findings.suggested_repair: Add to §4: 'If TB-28 = no, or for any timeout, C-3's "finish or time out" is recorded only as the run's stopped Event. The step itself stays nonterminal in the native record. This departs from the approved card wording and goes back to Jared as a C-3 note, recorded with the C-3 DL entry, as T-24 does.' Keep TB-28 with the owners too.

findings.claim: A consequence for Jared's approved C-2 answer is missed. C-2 says a Pause-origin stop is 'resumable later through replan'. Under ruling (c), such a stopped run can keep non-terminal attempts. A Replan must settle the effect census, invalidate the old generation, and give every affected WorkNode a 'cancelled' or 'resteered' disposition. The writers for those (record_invalidation, record_cancellation) remain dependency-only in v8, and v9 carries v8. So a census-only stop adds a constraint on the later replanned contract that neither T-25 nor the note records.
findings.verified_evidence: cards-C2-C4-20260925.md line 30: 'Pause is stopped and resumable later through replan.' replan/protocol.md @A1 line 72: 'rechecks all complete original sources, settled release/effect census, old-generation invalidation'. Line 153: 'node_of: D ↔ A must be a total bijection: one genuine cancelled|resteered record per affected WorkNode'. EP-125 @A1 8733-8735: record_cancellation, record_invalidation and apply_graph_lock 'stay complete dependency contracts only under EP-117'. EP-126 @A1 8825-8826: Replan native application 'is unavailable until the graph-lock owner''s participation is separately established'.
findings.suggested_repair: Add a line to T-25 (for A3-replanned): a Pause-origin stopped run may hold non-terminal attempts left by the census-only stop, and a resume through replan must dispose of them through owners v9 does not install. Mention it in the C-2 DL note as a limit on 'resumable later'.

findings.claim: Two lifecycle exits and one gap are not covered. (1) The Replan writer: nv8 129 says the combined profile permits a 'bounded replacement first-attempt chain', and a new RequiredSet chooses which members are required. So 'one attempt per step' holds only per WorkNode, and 'a required WorkNode failed' must be read against the current generation's RequiredSet. This is moot while Replan native application is unavailable, but v9's Replan release is still open (Q-V9-03). (2) DL-081: Jared approved a verification-exception finish for a run that 'cannot clear one check'. v9 births can never get that route later, because there is no late enrollment. The card should say so. (3) The §3.4 table has no row for a Goal resumed while the stop is still pending. The Goal Stop lasts only 'until the user explicitly resumes'. After a resume, W-C refuses (no latch) and W-B's no-Stop condition holds again.
findings.verified_evidence: nv8 129 @A1: 'The combined profile supplies the independently owned original Replan writer … and permits its bounded replacement first-attempt chain.' replan/protocol.md 63 @A1: 'The current RequiredSet selects current required members; it does not erase old failure'. Decision_Log.md 1647 @main (DL-081): 'Without a route, a run that cannot clear one check stays unfinished until someone cancels it', answered option 1 (route kept, contract not landed). EP-125 @A1 8700: 'there is no late or old-birth enrollment'. GRS 511 @main: a Stop defeats continuation 'until the user explicitly resumes'. Addendum §2.3 input 2: W-C 'refuses without it'.
findings.suggested_repair: Scope the W-B trigger and TB-02 to the current generation's RequiredSet (prop.). Add one line to card B-1: v9 runs whose check fails can never use the approved exception route of DL-081. Add a §3.4 row: 'Goal resumed while the stop is pending'. Its outcome depends on T-03 and T-24.

findings.claim: Citation and support details. (1) The note cites wam 761 ('COMPLETE_DEPENDENCY_DECLARATION_NOT_CURRENT_ACTIVATION_DISPATCH') as a reason record_failed is outside v8. The same label is on every native method in wam, including those v8 admits, so only EP-125 8733 tells them apart. (2) §2.2 cites 'nwca 2305-2380', while §1.2 cites 2277-2380. The definition starts at 2277. (3) Ruling (a), census by live facts rather than lifecycle, has canon support the note does not use: in canon, cancellation is recorded as an observation that keeps the lifecycle value. So an attempt can be settled while its lifecycle stays non-terminal (by analogy).
findings.verified_evidence: wam.json 742 (record_verified), 709 (begin_attempt) and 725 (submit_verification) carry the same activation_selection as 761. EP-125 @A1 8733: 'No v8 map or occurrence names owner.executor.native.record_failed.v1'. nwca StateTransitionReceipt starts at line 2277. wam 795 (record_cancellation): 'keep canonical lifecycle enum; no overwrite of prior terminal truth'. replan/protocol.md 155 @A1: 'WorkNode lifecycle remains queued/in_progress/verify_pending/verified/done/failed. Cancellation/invalidation remain separate full observations.'
findings.suggested_repair: Drop wam 761 as discriminating evidence and keep EP-125 8733. Align the nwca range. Cite wam 795 and replanP 155 under ruling (a) as 'by analogy' support.
